# The Problem With Current fMRI Pipelines

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}

Currently the fMRI pipelines are becoming more and more computationally heavy leveraging a lot of high dimension calculations.

However, there are several settings introducing noise instability in those pipelines:

- The OS running the pipeline and its version
- The actual hardware (CPU architecture)
- Parallelization strategies

:::

::: {.column width="40%"}

![Example of the same program giving different results depending on the OS](../assets/presentations/final-presentation/os_result_difference.png){#fig-os-results}

:::

::::

# Approach


We can artificially introduce numerical perturbations via Monte Carlo Arithmetic (MCA)(@Parker1997MonteCA) and assess how the desired pipeline's results change to make sure it is stable.

MCA introduces controlled random perturbations to floating-point operations during execution. By repeatedly running the same pipeline, we can quantify how numerical variability propagates.

Tools that implement this:

- [Verificarlo](https://github.com/verificarlo/verificarlo){target="_blank"}(@denis2018verificarlocheckingfloatingpoint): compiler wrapper that instruments floating point operations at the LLVM level

- [Fuzzy](https://github.com/verificarlo/fuzzy){target="_blank"}(@greg_kiar_2026_20906259): Docker ecosystem with pre-instrumented versions of common numerical libraries (NumPy, SciPy) so you can evaluate a pipeline's stability without recompiling


# Previous Work in Neuroimaging

Numerical variability has been studied across several neuroimaging domains:

- Functional imaging: @Alizadeh2025.12.22.695524 evaluated the Numerical Population Variability Ratio (NPVR) of graph metrics (0.1-0.2 range), varying across brain regions and thresholds
- Structural imaging: @Chatelain2026.01.09.698203 found numerical variation reached ~1/3 of population variability in Parkinson's
- Diffusion imaging: @kiar2021 showed different computational environments produce substantially different connectivity results

Numerical variability as augmentation: @gonzalezpepe2026fuzzypytorchrapidnumerical showed controlled perturbations can serve as data augmentation for deep learning

However, stability conclusions cannot be generalized across pipelines due to heterogeneous methodologies. Benchmarking each pipeline is essential.


# Contributions

This thesis, conducted in collaboration with Advanced Telecommunications Research Institute International (ATR), investigated the numerical stability of fMRI connectivity biomarkers.

This work was divided into three complementary parts:

1. Reproduce the @Alizadeh2025.12.22.695524 analysis of MRI graph metrics using the Numerical Population Variability Ratio (NPVR)
2. Extend the analysis to edge-wise FC matrix stability, including the effect of global signal regression
3. Assess the numerical stability of PCA-based feature selection (@10.1162/IMAG.a.1121) under perturbations

# @Alizadeh2025.12.22.695524 Paper Goals

The paper has two goals:

 - Demonstrate on artificial data that NPVR increases uncertainty in Cohen's $d$ estimates, with stronger effects at small sample sizes.
 - Assess how numerical perturbations via Verificarlo of fMRIPrep runs impact the NPVR of various graph metrics.

Here is the formula for the NPVR:

$$NPVR = \frac{\sigma_{num}}{\sigma_{pop}}$$

Where $\sigma_{num}$ is the numerical variability and $\sigma_{pop}$ is the population variability.

# @Alizadeh2025.12.22.695524 Graph Metrics

Here are the different graph metrics that were computed once with and once without confounds regression

The FC matrices were computed using the Schaefer 2018 parcellation with 100 cortical regions and 7 functional networks.

Four local graph metrics were computed:

  - Degree centrality
  - Clustering coefficient
  - Betweenness centrality
  - Eigenvector centrality

Two global metrics:

  - Small-worldness
  - Average shortest path length

# Graph Metrics Reproduction Methodology

This reproduction differed from the original study in several ways:

- Different dataset: Used the [BMB dataset](https://mridata-brainminds-beyond.atr.jp/dataset/bmbpt/) (@KOIKE2021102600) instead of the original [PPMI dataset](https://www.ppmi-info.org/access-data-specimens/download-data) (@marek2018)
- More confounds: Applied 15 confounds (vs original 6), adding global signal, CSF, white matter, and 6 aCompCor components
- Custom Docker container: Built a custom fMRIPrep 25.2.5 container (vs Fuzzy's 23.2.1)
- Small-worldness was excluded due to computational constraints

# @10.1162/IMAG.a.1121 PCA Feature Selection Stability Analysis

The goal of this paper is to develop a PCA-based feature selection method that robustly extracts reliable FC biomarkers
for major depressive disorder (MDD), schizophrenia (SCZ), and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) across
multiple independent datasets and imaging sites, overcoming the instability issues of conventional supervised feature selection approaches.

# Original PCA Feature Selection Explanation

The PCA feature selection works as follows:

- A PCA is computed on all subjects' FC vector to reduce dimensionality to n principal components.
- PCs are tested for association with variables of interest:
  - Binary categorical (e.g., diagnosis, sex): two-sample t-test
  - Multi-level categorical (e.g., imaging site): one-way ANOVA
  - Continuous (e.g., age, BDI, head motion): Pearson's correlation
- Select PCs significantly associated with the target after FDR-BH correction (q < 0.05)
- Test FC weights using a chi-squared test with FDR-BH correction (q < 0.05)
- Keep only FCs that survive the correction as the final biomarkers

# PCA Feature Selection Improvements

I made several changes to the PCA feature selection code:

 - Transformed the repository from regular Python code to a Python package (see PR [here](https://github.com/Ayumu722/pca-based-feature-extraction/pull/1){target="_blank"})
 - Improved the PC plots (see PR [here](https://github.com/Ayumu722/pca-based-feature-extraction/pull/3){target="_blank"})

# PCA Feature Selection Stability Analysis Procedure

To conduct this analysis, I performed the following steps:

- Reproduced the PCA feature selection on the complete SRPB dataset (@Tanaka2021) and on the BMB dataset (a new dataset)
- Perturbation 1: Ran 100 (SRPB) and 15 (BMB) perturbed FC matrix extractions via MCA-instrumented `np.corrcoef`
- Perturbation 2: Reduced PCA inputs precision from 64-bit [double precision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-precision_floating-point_format) to 32-bit [single precision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-precision_floating-point_format)

The PCA feature selection was applied to each perturbed run to assess stability

# Conclusion

This thesis investigated numerical stability of fMRI connectivity biomarkers across three complementary analyses:

1. Graph metrics NPVR: Reproduced Alizadeh et al. on the [BMB dataset](https://mridata-brainminds-beyond.atr.jp/dataset/bmbpt/) with 15 confounds (vs original 6). Found broadly consistent trends but higher NPVR values. Confound regression effect was more variable across thresholds and metrics

2. Edge-wise FC matrix NPVR: ~11% mean NPVR across 4950 edges. Without global signal confound, NPVR more than doubles

3. PCA feature extraction: Fully robust under combined MCA perturbation of `np.corrcoef` and 32-bit PCA precision

Key takeaway: While FC matrices and derived graph metrics show measurable numerical variability, the PCA-based biomarker extraction pipeline is highly numerically stable.

# Future Directions

- Assess individual confound contributions to NPVR
- Perturb the cross-site harmonization step
- Perturb confound regression process itself

# Annex
Here is how the NPVR is calculated in details:

$$
  \sigma_{num}^2 = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{j=1}^m \left[ \frac{1}{n-1} \sum_{i=1}^n \left( x_{i,j} - \bar x_{.,j}\right)^2\right]
$$

$$
  \sigma_{pop}^2 = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \left[ \frac{1}{m-1} \sum_{j=1}^m \left( x_{i,j} - \bar x_{i,.}\right)^2\right]
$$

$$
  NPVR = \frac{\sigma_{num}}{\sigma_{pop}}
$$
